title: Compatibility guardrails, LTS branching, and progressive upgrade tooling for serving runtime
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Establish a prescriptive semantic versioning and LTS strategy for the serving runtime that minimizes customer disruption while enabling continuous improvement. Deliverables: (1) a short, enforceable semver policy for runtime consumers and internal teams; (2) an LTS branching and backport cadence; (3) rollout gates and automated checks to catch compatibility regressions; (4) a lightweight upgrade CLI and migration guidance for operators; (5) documentation and communication templates for customers.
semver_policy_summary: Runtime versions will follow MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. MAJOR increments indicate breaking changes to on-disk or RPC/API contracts (including wire formats, config keys, and plugin ABI). MINOR increments add backwards-compatible features and behavior improvements. PATCH increments are bug fixes/backports only. Deprecations must be announced at least one MINOR cycle before removal. No breaking changes are allowed in an existing MAJOR branch without an opt-in compatibility flag and an explicit migration plan.
deprecation_and_removal_process: When an API or behavior is deprecated: 1) Add deprecation metadata to server responses and SDKs; 2) Publish a deprecation note in the changelog and release notes; 3) Create a migration guide and test fixtures; 4) Mark for removal in a planned future MAJOR version (with exact version in release notes). Deprecations require compatibility tests and at least one MINOR release of overlap before removal.
lts_branching_policy: Designate stable MAJOR.x.y lines as LTS for 12 months (configurable per major). LTS branches receive security and critical bug backports (PATCH and select MINOR-level performance fixes) only. Backport requests must go through the staging compatibility suite and have approvals from Release Engineering and Runtime Owners. LTS promotion criteria: stable for 6 consecutive weeks, <1% customer-facing error rate, passing perf regressions.
compatibility_checks_and_gate_automation: Introduce a mandatory compatibility matrix check in CI for any change touching transports, config, on-disk formats, or public interfaces. The check runs: - API contract tests (integration against latest SDKs) - Golden KV cache snapshots comparison - Feature-flagged compatibility runs across the last two MINOR releases and current HEAD. Failures block merge until either a shim is added or the change is gated and documented.
rollout_gates: Release gating will include: 1) CI compatibility green; 2) Performance gate (no >10% tail latency regression on representative workloads); 3) Canary plan with incremental percentage rollout automated via the console; 4) Automated rollback trigger on elevated errors/latency. Gate owners: Change author (primary), Release Engineering (final), SRE (canary monitoring).
upgrade_tooling_notes: Deliver a runtime-upgrade CLI (runtimectl) with commands: plan, preview, apply, rollback. 'plan' shows potential incompatible config keys and recommended automatic migrations. 'preview' runs compatibility checks against a test cluster using snapshot data. The tool will surface human-readable remediation steps and produce a machine-readable migration manifest for automation. Include an SDK compatibility validator used by our package builds.
canary_and_rollback_strategy: Use staged canaries: dev -> internal -> 1% external -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Each stage must meet health/latency/SLO checks for a configurable window. Rollback is automated on thresholds (error rate delta, latency spikes, or regression in correctness tests). Rollbacks should be fast (under 15 minutes median) and tested monthly.
documentation_and_communications: Maintain a single 'Runtime Compatibility & Upgrade' doc in Confluence with: changelog guidance, deprecation timeline template, customer-facing notification templates, and step-by-step upgrade runbooks. Release notes must include compatibility impact summary and links to migration guides. Notify Dedicated/Private customers with scheduled upgrade windows and opt-out mechanics.
decision_log: Chosen to enforce semantic guarantees at the runtime boundary (RPC/config/format) rather than internal refactors to reduce customer confusion. Rejected model where every MINOR may contain breaking opt-in changes because it caused unpredictable operator burden in preliminary experiments. Trade-offs: stricter semver slows introduction of certain performance-breaking optimizations; mitigation = allow opt-in compatibility flags and experimental channels.
acceptance_criteria: - Publish policy doc and ship a CI compatibility check that runs on PRs touching public interfaces. - Runtimectl v0.1 with plan/preview commands and basic incompatibility detection in PR environment. - Canary automation configured and runbook published. - LTS promotion checklist accepted by Release Engineering.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Performance improvements that require ABI changes may be delayed. Mitigation: support experimental MAJOR-preview builds and compatibility shims. Risk: customers may miss deprecation notices. Mitigation: add deprecation headers to responses and targeted emails for Dedicated/Private customers.
follow_up_tasks: Create CI job definition for compatibility matrix (ENG-34103)
notes: This ticket is intentionally scoped to policy and minimal tooling prototypes. Full migration automation and large-scale backports will be separate follow-ups. Coordinate with Product and Support for customer-facing messaging.
